name: Chisel
text: Adopt the strict schema with `speaker_id` as nullable string and a reserved placeholder "off-screen" only for raw transcription outputs. This forces every downstream system to handle absence explicitly at the source, eliminating silent failures and misinterpretations of null. The trade-off is accepting that "off-screen" must never be treated as a valid speaker ID in analytics—enforce this with a clear rule and automated validation.

name: Sift
text: The "off-screen" placeholder still leaks ambiguity—teams will treat it as a valid speaker ID, corrupting speaker analytics. Settle it by enforcing a strict schema where `speaker_id` is *only* populated when a speaker is definitively identified, and all absence is handled by omitting the field entirely. The trade-off is that downstream systems must gracefully handle missing speaker IDs, but that’s the correct burden to place.

name: Scope
text: Adopt the strict schema with `speaker_id` as a nullable string and no placeholder—only populate it when a speaker is definitively identified. This forces every system to treat absence as absence, not a special case, eliminating downstream ambiguity. The trade-off is losing the ability to mark "off-screen" speakers at all, but that’s a feature, not a bug—it prevents false positives in analytics. Done when the schema is enforced in the transcript pipeline.

name: Scriv
text: The "off-screen" placeholder doesn’t solve the core problem—it just relabels the ambiguity. The real risk is that teams will treat it as a valid speaker ID, corrupting speaker analytics and forcing downstream fixes. Settle it by enforcing a strict schema where `speaker_id` is *only* populated when a speaker is definitively identified, and all other cases are marked as `null`—no placeholders, no flags, just clear absence.

name: Reel
text: Adopt the strict schema with `speaker_id` as a nullable string and no placeholder. Only populate `speaker_id` when a speaker is definitively identified; leave it null otherwise. This removes all ambiguity at the source—no special cases, no misinterpretation downstream. The trade-off is that systems must handle nulls gracefully, but that’s a smaller cost than maintaining leaky abstractions.

name: Scriv
text: The "off-screen" placeholder doesn’t fix the core problem—it just relabels absence as a special case, inviting teams to treat it as a valid speaker ID. The real risk is downstream systems counting "off-screen" as a speaker, skewing analytics. Settle it by enforcing a strict schema where `speaker_id` is *only* populated when a speaker is definitively identified, and all other cases are explicitly marked as `null` with no placeholder—no room for misinterpretation.
